athenaOutput.directive: Transform the Creative Liberation Engine's user interaction model from a 'building block' approach to an 'outcome-driven' paradigm, enabling users to articulate high-level goals which the system then intelligently translates into orchestrated agent workflows and dynamically generated interfaces.
athenaOutput.rationale: The Home Assistant 2026.6 release demonstrates a powerful shift in UX design: guiding users by their desired outcome rather than requiring them to understand underlying components. This 'entity-first' or 'purpose-specific' approach, combined with live previews and enhanced transparency, significantly lowers the barrier to entry and inspires creativity. For the Creative Liberation Engine, this means moving beyond manual agent selection and configuration towards a system that proactively suggests and orchestrates agents and workflows based on user intent, making the complex process of AI system design intuitive and accessible. This aligns with Article XX: Zero human wait time, by automating the 'how' for the user.

options.title: Outcome-Driven Agent Orchestrator
options.description: Shift the core interaction of the Creative Liberation Engine to an outcome-first model. Users describe a desired goal or outcome (e.g., 'Analyze market trends and generate a summary report'), and the Creative Liberation Engine intelligently suggests, configures, and orchestrates the optimal agents and workflows to achieve it. This is analogous to Home Assistant's card picker suggesting UI based on the entity, but applied to agent systems.
options.tradeoffs: High architectural complexity due to the need for sophisticated semantic parsing, dynamic workflow generation, and robust agent capability mapping. Requires extensive initial knowledge base population for agents. Benefits include significantly reduced user friction and accelerated workflow creation. Design challenge lies in making the 'intelligent suggestion' process transparent and editable.
options.architecture: Develop a 'Goal-to-Agent Mapper' service that leverages KEEPER for agent capabilities and semantic understanding. Implement a dynamic workflow generation engine that can compose multi-agent interactions. Integrate with RELAY for intelligent routing and AURORA for architectural validation of proposed workflows. Requires a robust metadata system for agent functions and data schemas. BOLT would be activated to generate the executable workflow code.
options.design: A conversational UI or a 'Goal Canvas' where users state their objectives in natural language. Live previews of the proposed agent workflow, visualizing data flow, agent responsibilities, and expected outputs. An interactive 'workflow blueprint' that dynamically updates as the goal is refined, allowing for visual adjustments and configuration. Clear visual indicators for agent status and progress within the orchestrated task.

options.title: Semantic Component Studio with Live Previews
options.description: Create an Creative Liberation Engine component studio that suggests UI elements, data connectors, or agent interfaces based on the data context or agent output schema, with live previews using actual or simulated data. This mirrors Home Assistant's card picker, but for the Creative Liberation Engine's internal and external-facing components.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant effort in creating a comprehensive component registry and data schema mapping. Live preview functionality can be resource-intensive. Benefits include accelerated UI/UX development and a more intuitive component selection process. Custom component integration requires a well-defined API.
options.architecture: A 'Schema-to-Component Matcher' service that queries a KEEPER-managed component registry, storing metadata about UI components and their data requirements. Develop real-time data simulation/sampling capabilities for rendering live previews. Implement a pluggable architecture for custom components, allowing BOLT to generate compatible code. Ensure robust API for data binding and component configuration.
options.design: A 'By Data Source' or 'By Agent Output' tab in a component picker. A hierarchical view of available data schemas or agent output types. The right-hand pane displays live-rendered previews of suitable UI components, populated with sample data from the selected source. Implement glassmorphic design elements for a modern, transparent aesthetic. Ensure mobile-responsive design for flexible component building.

options.title: Transparent Workflow Debugger & Auditor
options.description: Build an advanced debugging and auditing interface for Creative Liberation Engine workflows and agent interactions, offering real-time visualization of data flow, condition evaluation, and resource targeting. This directly translates Home Assistant's automation editor enhancements (live indicators, target counts, notes).
options.tradeoffs: Requires a robust, high-performance logging and tracing infrastructure. Data visualization for complex multi-agent systems can be challenging. Benefits include increased trust, easier debugging, and improved operational transparency. Potential performance overhead during active debugging.
options.architecture: Implement a centralized, high-fidelity logging and tracing service that captures all agent interactions, data transformations, and condition evaluations. Develop a 'Workflow Execution Graph' generator for runtime visualization. Integrate VERA for truth validation at each step. Design a metadata storage system for inline notes/annotations on workflow steps. IRIS provides the real-time execution context.
options.design: A 'debugger' view for workflows, displaying execution paths, data payloads at each node, and real-time pass/fail indicators for conditional logic. Implement a 'target count' overlay on agents or data sinks, showing processed items/entities. Provide interactive annotations and notes directly on the workflow canvas. Include a timeline view for historical execution analysis and replay.

options.title: Universal Event Listener & Protocol Bridge
options.description: Develop a robust, universal event listening system that can ingest signals from a vast array of physical and digital protocols (e.g., IR, Matter, Zigbee, Flipper Zero, webhooks, API calls), translating them into standardized Creative Liberation Engine events. This expands the Creative Liberation Engine's sensory input, mirroring Home Assistant's Infrared listening.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant engineering effort to develop and maintain numerous protocol integrations. Security implications of interfacing with diverse external systems must be meticulously managed (LEX). Benefits include vastly expanded input capabilities and broader integration possibilities. Complexity in standardizing disparate event formats.
options.architecture: Design a 'Protocol Bridge' agent (SIGNAL) capable of interfacing with various hardware/software protocols, including specific support for Flipper Zero as a multi-protocol sensor/transmitter. Establish a standardized internal event bus for Creative Liberation Engine events. Implement an event processing pipeline for filtering, transforming, and routing events to relevant agents or workflows. Ensure robust error handling and security measures.
options.design: An 'Event Stream Visualizer' showing incoming events, their source, type, and payload in real-time. A user-friendly mapping interface to associate external events with internal Creative Liberation Engine actions or triggers. Configurable dashboards for monitoring event traffic, system responsiveness, and potential security alerts. Visual cues for active and inactive listeners.

options.title: Community-Driven Component & Agent Marketplace
options.description: Establish a curated, community-driven marketplace for Creative Liberation Engine components (UI elements, data connectors, agent skills, workflow templates), complete with robust developer tooling and a clear 'opt-in' mechanism for integration with core Creative Liberation Engine features. This emulates Home Assistant's custom card integration.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant infrastructure for a marketplace, including security, versioning, and moderation. Legal and compliance considerations for third-party code (LEX). Benefits include accelerated ecosystem growth and increased functionality. Quality control and maintenance of community contributions can be challenging.
options.architecture: Implement a secure, sandboxed environment for running community-contributed agents/components. Develop a version control system and a robust API for developers to register their components, specifying capabilities and schemas. Integrate with KEEPER for managing component metadata. Establish a review and moderation process, potentially involving LEX for compliance checks. BOLT could assist in generating marketplace templates.
options.design: A discoverable 'Marketplace' UI within the Creative Liberation Engine, featuring clear categorization, search, and filtering. Provide detailed documentation, usage examples, and code snippets for each contribution. Implement rating and review systems. Use visual indicators to distinguish official Creative Liberation Engine components from community contributions. A clear 'Developer Portal' for submission and management.
